articleBlocks: Horn and Cod immediately felt like place names, but not yet like one clean category. The opening clues stay ambiguous until Of Good Hope gives the board a cleaner test, so this guide starts with the misleading first read, then uses the later clues to show why the final connection is narrower than the early guesses and how each clue checks that same pattern without relying on the answer reveal too early.

fullAnalysis: Horn and Cod immediately felt like place names, but not yet like one clean category.

Of Good Hope was the clue that changed the solve because that phrase almost always appears with Cape in front of it.
Once that completion surfaced, Horn, Cod, Verde, and Canaveral all turned into exact geographic names: Cape Horn, Cape Cod, Cape Verde, and Cape Canaveral.

solutionNarrative: Horn, Cod, and Verde pulled me toward famous place names, which was close enough to feel promising but too broad to solve the board. Canaveral helped, but it still could have been filed under general landmarks or travel geography.

The board finally locked when Of Good Hope appeared. That phrase made Cape unavoidable, and once that missing word surfaced, every earlier clue became an exact named cape instead of a loose map reference.
